memoryReview.lesson: Its geographic field is the entire strategic object; Crown Laws instead keeps one bounded 5×7 stone tabletop and a fixed hand of decrees.

memoryReview.lesson: Painting and canvas tools dominate ZAMAZKA; Crown Laws must show legal decisions before tools or flourishes, with pieces moving automatically.

references.observation: The Met documents medieval book covers using precious materials and strong geometric surfaces rather than floating interface ornaments.
references.principle: Use compact material boundaries to distinguish the legal decree object from its surrounding stone institution.
references.application: Rectangular parchment law cards use ink-like text and a thin stamped faction strip instead of illustrated backgrounds.
references.avoid: Do not reproduce specific manuscript pages, monograms, protected imagery or decorative initial drawings.

references.observation: V&A discusses Gothic objects crossing from architecture to three-dimensional sculpture with distinct material edges.
references.principle: A frame should behave like carved physical support around the royal game, not a generic translucent card.
references.application: The playfield uses a thick bevelled stone surround, measured cells and strong unbroken rectangular panel edges.
references.avoid: Avoid building an illegible ornamental cathedral facade over the usable interactive board.

references.observation: The British Library records the Lansdowne Psalter with framed miniatures and deliberate gold, orange and blue distinctions.
references.principle: Restrained colored detail can communicate function while retaining the seriousness of medieval record keeping.
references.application: The North and South counters have separate blue and red material rings; bronze focuses primary decree confirmation.
references.avoid: Do not borrow actual manuscript miniatures or treat decorative colors as interchangeable game-state labels.

concepts.medium: HTML/CSS geometric stone slab, paper legal cards and code-drawn stamped counters with no runtime image atlas.
concepts.composition: The board and live law ledger form a two-column council on desktop; a compact hand follows the board on phone.
concepts.interaction: Choose a decree tile, see the complete description directly below the hand, then confirm the hidden law choice.
concepts.motion: Measured selected-card lift and per-cell linear token travel; short highlights punctuate clashes rather than covering the grid.
concepts.rationale: This preserves the simultaneous hidden decree mechanic while replacing old decorative clutter with a spatially stable interface.

concepts.medium: A bespoke canvas renderer with hand-placed sculptural pseudo-relief and carved ornamental individual miniatures.
concepts.composition: The battlefield fills the scene as one altar stone while tiny side plaques hide available current laws and cards.
concepts.interaction: Players drag embossed coins from an arc surrounding the board into a central slot to submit hidden commands.
concepts.motion: Heavily eased rotations and carved-piece swells would make each resolution ceremonial and comparatively slow.
concepts.rationale: Its strong theatrical model introduces gesture-dependent controls that would bury readable decrees on a small screen.

concepts.medium: Multi-page CSS folio instrument with stitched side margins, codex gutters and text-first ink panels.
concepts.composition: Each gameplay layer is a separate full-screen folio: board page, law book page, decree page and chronicle page.
concepts.interaction: Users flip between folios to examine individual acts and apply a decree from a compact bottom page tab.
concepts.motion: A page-turn sequence and layered parchment scroll would organize navigation around document transitions.
concepts.rationale: It makes room for long legal prose but repeatedly obscures the shared board precisely when laws are being evaluated.

concepts.medium: Original hand-authored SVG vector portrait sheet, law seals and two ceremonial illustrations; editable sources live in asset-forge/ and published SVG files in assets/.
concepts.composition: Hall illustration anchors the menu; six illustrated actor tokens animate on a flat 5x7 field; five color-locked heraldic seals tag laws; a victory insignia replaces text-only end-state.
concepts.interaction: All cards and laws are actionable. Debug screen preview offers read-only state interaction. Conditional turn forecast comes from pure engine simulation.
concepts.motion: Brief wax seal, crown highlights, board move and victory reveal, all reducible.
concepts.rationale: Distinct vector silhouette vocabulary corrects the geometric-only placeholder look without sacrificing rules legibility.

selection.reason: Original manuscript vector plates depict actors and ceremony, while keeping board and law mechanics directly accessible.

rejected.reason: Full sculptural 2.5D view deferred; field remains flat and legible.

tools.reason: Original browser HTML and CSS provide all board, token, material and feedback geometry without generated SVG or picture tiles.
A deterministic Node image routine draws the product crown onto an isolated pixel buffer and serializes one PNG for the app icon.

Four editable SVG sources and matching publishable SVG vectors are checked in, alongside an Art Forge v2 vector production plan. Do not activate manifest.json until required Inkscape PNG exports and hash index are built and committed.

assets.role: Unique app launch emblem combining rough cut stone and a high contrast gold crown for the Pocket Works launcher.
assets.acceptance: The new icon remains recognizable at 48 pixels and the old SVG install graphics are absent from the application tree.
assets.integration: Manifest and HTML reference only the local icon PNG; service worker caches exactly the new standalone icon and no gameplay textures.
assets.provenance: Pixels are drawn by an original project-local deterministic raster script rather than sourced illustration or downloaded sprite.
